challenges.title: Opening an account takes two or more visits
challenges.problem: Customers arrive without the right documents and are asked to come back. Some never return.
challenges.why: Lost new accounts and repeat queue time at busy lounges.

challenges.title: Card replacement requests are handled on paper forms
challenges.problem: Forms are filled at the counter, scanned and re-keyed by the back office, so replacements take days.
challenges.affects: Card customers, lounge and card operations staff
challenges.why: Slow turnaround, keying errors and repeat visits to check status.

challenges.title: Loan applicants can't see where their application stands
challenges.problem: Applicants call or visit repeatedly to ask for status updates.
challenges.affects: Loan customers, lounge and credit staff
challenges.why: Staff time lost to status calls; poor customer experience.

challenges.title: Atoll customers travel to Malé for simple requests
challenges.problem: Some requests still need an in-person signature or a visit to a main branch.
challenges.why: Travel cost and time for customers; lost goodwill.

challenges.title: Complaints are tracked on spreadsheets
challenges.problem: There is no single view of open complaints or how long each has been open.

challenges.title: Customers queue for simple requests like statements and PIN resets
challenges.problem: Every request takes a queue ticket, however simple it is.
challenges.why: Long waits put off customers who came for advice or a sale.

whys: Customers are asked to come back to complete the account opening.
They are missing one or more required documents.
They did not know which documents to bring.
The list is not shared before the visit.
There is no step that contacts the customer before they arrive.
work.root: No pre-visit step tells customers exactly which documents they need.
work.title: Ready Before You Arrive
work.approach: Send a document checklist by SMS and Viber the moment a customer books or enquires, with a one-tap pre-check of their ID.
work.impl: Template messages in 2 weeks; pilot in two Malé lounges for a month; Retail owns the rollout.
work.benefits: Most new accounts opened in one visit; fewer repeat queue tickets at peak hours.

whys: Card replacements take several days.
Each request is keyed in twice.
The paper form is scanned and re-entered by the back office.
The lounge has no screen to raise the request directly.
The process was designed before the digital workflow existed.
work.root: Requests start on paper because there is no direct digital entry at the lounge.
work.title: Card in a Click
work.approach: A simple digital request screen at the lounge that sends card replacements straight to card operations.
work.impl: Use the existing workflow tool; build the form in 3 weeks; pilot with one lounge.
work.benefits: Turnaround from days to hours; no re-keying errors.

whys: Applicants call to ask about their loan.
They don't know what stage it is at.
Nobody tells them when it moves forward.
Status changes are not linked to customer messages.
Customer updates are not owned by any team.
work.root: No one owns telling the applicant when their loan moves to the next stage.
work.title: Track My Loan
work.approach: Automatic status messages at each loan stage: received, under review, approved, ready to sign.
work.impl: Map the stages with Credit; trigger SMS from the existing loan workflow; pilot on personal loans.
work.benefits: Fewer status calls to lounges and credit; better customer satisfaction.

whys: Atoll customers travel to Malé.
Some requests need a wet signature.
The policy requires the signature to be witnessed.
Remote identity checks are not accepted for these requests.
The policy has not been reviewed since video verification became possible.
work.root: Policy still requires in-person signatures where a remote check would be enough.
work.title: Bank From Your Island
work.approach: Video-verified requests for the most common atoll visits, signed digitally.
work.impl: Agree the request list with Compliance; pilot video verification in two atolls.
work.benefits: Less travel for customers; fewer walk-ins at the main branch.

whys: Complaints are resolved slowly.
Managers can't see which complaints are overdue.
Each lounge keeps its own spreadsheet.
There is no shared complaint log.
No standard complaint process has been set up across lounges.
work.root: There is no shared complaint log with owners and due dates.
work.title: One Complaints View
work.approach: A shared complaint log with an owner and a due date for every complaint, and a weekly overdue list.
work.impl: Start on a shared form and dashboard; train lounge managers in one session.
work.benefits: Faster resolution and fewer repeat complaints.

whys: Customers wait a long time for simple requests.
Simple and complex requests share one queue.
The ticket machine has a single service type.
Queues were set up for transactions, not service requests.
Nobody has reviewed which requests could be self-service.
work.root: Simple requests share one queue with complex ones and have no self-service option.
work.title: Fast Lane
work.approach: A self-service kiosk and a quick-service desk for statements, PIN and card requests.
work.impl: Pilot one kiosk at the busiest lounge; add a quick-service ticket type; review after six weeks.
work.benefits: Shorter queues and more advisor time for sales conversations.
